_comment: SP-066: the image pick's rubric, read by lib/pick.js (Jev), shaped like scripts/story-rubric.json's axes. One Score question per scored cell and axis; Jev answers a level 0-2, and the axis score is that + 1 (decimals kept, as US-038 keeps them). An axis's optional "check" is added to its question. SP-066 changes SP-064's rubric in two places only (ADR-0033): vivid scores the scene (what the story objects do to each other), not the camera, with the angle exception of C-042; and must-see clarity uses each item's size from the caption, so a small item gets the lowest level. Must-see clarity still checks the items with their adjectives (ADR-0032). After stage 2, the plausible and clarity checks name the drawing errors (ADR-0036) and the name sign (ADR-0035), so that Jev's levels agree with the caps that lib/pick.js applies in code.

plausible.label: Plausible
levels: the scene makes little sense: no setting clues, or the action happens in an order that doesn't fit the story
the scene makes some sense: a few setting clues, or a mostly sensible order of action
the scene makes sense: clear setting clues such as a floor, a hand or a height, and a sensible order of action
plausible.check: A drawing error (an object in the cell's drawing_errors: it floats, looks pasted on, or breaks the lines of the wall or floor) makes the scene make less sense: one on a must-see item gives the lowest level, and one on another object gives the middle level at most.

vivid.label: Vivid
vivid.check: Score the scene, not the camera: what the story objects do to each other, from the cell's action line and the sizes of its must-see items. An eye-level, medium shot is the normal view, and an extreme close-up or a strong camera angle adds nothing. An unusual camera angle lowers vivid only when it hides the action; an unusual angle never lowers vivid when the state's angle_case is "view" (the story is about a view) or "one-object" (the story has one main object).
levels: the story objects are small, far away or apart from each other
the story objects are clear, but they don't act on each other as the story says
the story objects are large and act on each other as the story says

clarity.label: Must-see clarity
clarity.check: Check each must-see item with its adjectives: the item must be shown in the state its adjectives give (a bare cob). The cell's must-see marks say whether the item itself is visible, partly cut or hidden, and give its size (large / medium / small) and place (front / back); they don't check its state. Use each item's size: a small item gets the lowest level. A name sign is not a must-see item: when the cell's name_sign_readable is false (its readable text doesn't show the name, such as "Venice" on the nurse's nametag), give the middle level at most.
levels: a must-see item is small, is partly cut off by the edge of the picture, or is not in the state its adjectives give (a cob that isn't bare yet)
every must-see item is shown in full and in the state its adjectives give, and none is small, but some are only medium or unclear, or a name sign can't be read (no "Venice" on the nurse's nametag)
every must-see item is shown in full, in the state its adjectives give, large and clear, and every name sign can be read
